minutes.headline: Finance Committee took no budget votes; heard town manager updates and discussed TC Passios timing and capital policy
minutes.summary: The committee heard the town manager's updates on grants, the FY21 tax rate, capital projects and early FY22 budget priorities. Members discussed a COLA-style contract policy, a land reserve fund idea from open space, TC Passios building reuse timing, and a rubric for evaluating major building projects. Minutes were put off for lack of review, and the meeting adjourned by roll call.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no votes; it heard the town manager report on grants, the FY21 tax rate, capital projects and early FY22 priorities.
The FY21 tax rate was reported as certified and lower than FY20's.
Approval of the October 8 minutes was put off until members have read them.
Evan agreed to serve as the committee's liaison to police and fire.
A capital threshold and fiscal policies were discussed and deferred to January, with the chair and Chris to prepare a major-building-project rubric.

why_it_matters: The tax rate, health insurance guidance and a likely trash contract increase feed the FY22 budget that residents will be asked to vote on at Town Meeting.
A capital threshold and a rubric for major building projects, including reuse of the TC Passios building, would set how future large projects are screened and funded.
watch_next: Next meeting January 14, 2021, with policy discussion as a standing agenda item.
The major-building-project rubric, due to be brought forward in January.
